title: Modular SDK starter skeletons: Next.js + FastAPI + Go + CLI (retries & streaming ergonomics)
creator: Ava Mitchell
description: Create a set of modular, production-oriented starter skeletons that demonstrate best-practice SDK usage across three runtimes (Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP server) plus a CLI example. Focus areas: idiomatic streaming ergonomics, robust retry/backoff strategies, resumable streaming patterns, and minimal but realistic app wiring (auth, config, examples). These should be small, copy-pasteable repos or folders with README-driven walkthroughs that can be used by developer advocates and customers to bootstrap apps quickly.
acceptance_criteria: Next.js example supports both SSR edge and serverless runtimes and demonstrates streaming tokens into a client-side streaming component (hydrated via event stream or fetch + ReadableStream)
FastAPI example exposes an async streaming endpoint and an example client that consumes token-by-token output using async for / async iterators
Go HTTP server example demonstrates context cancellation, graceful shutdown, and streaming using io.Reader style adapters plus a minimal Go client showing incremental processing
CLI example demonstrates resumable streaming (checkpointed output), exponential backoff with jitter for retries, and a --stream flag that yields tokens in real-time
All examples include a shared retry policy (configurable) and a short benchmarking script that measures latency and throughput for local dev
Docs contain clear instructions to wire examples to Redwood hosted API keys and to run locally with minimal dependencies
Automated tests cover streaming behavior, retry backoff logic, and a CI job runs lightweight smoke tests on PRs
tasks: Design skeletal repo structure (single mono-folder with language folders + shared README) and decide sample prompts/use-cases
Implement Next.js example with TypeScript: server route + client component; support edge-runtime and Node server runtime toggles
Implement FastAPI Python example: async streaming endpoint and example async client script
Implement Go example: http.Handler streaming response and client using context.Context cancellation
Implement CLI example (Python) with --stream and checkpoint resume behavior; integrate retry/backoff utility
Write reusable retry/backoff utilities in each language with same semantics documented
Add CI smoke tests that run each example in a container and validate token streaming semantics and retry behavior
Author READMEs, minimal architecture diagram, and a short troubleshooting FAQ
implementation_notes: Prefer small, dependency-light implementations. For Next.js use native fetch + ReadableStream for streaming; avoid heavy libraries so customers can adapt easily.
Streaming ergonomics guidance: provide both a high-level convenience hook/helper and a low-level streaming example to teach patterns.
Retry policy: provide an opinionated default (2 retries, exponential backoff starting at 200ms with full jitter) but surface a config object so teams can tune.
Resumable streaming: implement a simple append-only checkpoint file in CLI example and demonstrate how to reconcile partial results on resume.
Instrumentation: add a tiny sample of emitting per-request timing and token counts to stdout to illustrate latency/cost tradeoffs.
Compatibility: use the stable parts of the Redwood SDK surface (generation + streaming) and fallback to raw HTTP examples for teams not using the SDKs.
Tests: mock Redwood API in unit tests; CI smoke tests hit staging with a test API key stored in secrets manager
testing_plan: Unit tests for retry utilities (verify backoff schedule and jitter bounds)
Streaming unit tests using a mocked generator that yields partial chunks and simulates network hiccups
Integration smoke test that runs a short prompt and asserts that the full text reconstructs from streamed chunks
CLI resume test: simulate an interrupted stream, then resume and confirm no duplication and correct final output
CI job: run examples in ephemeral containers and run the smoke test suite on PRs to this folder
rollout_plan: Merge skeletons into examples/mono-repo branch behind a feature flag
Run a 1-week dogfood campaign with developer advocates to try the starters and collect friction points
Iterate on README and ergonomics based on feedback; finalize and tag release sdks-2025.03-examples
Announce to SDK changelog and link from SDK quickstarts in docs site
Monitor telemetry (downloads, repo clones, issues) and prepare a follow-up iteration for specific language ergonomics
